title: Broken streetlight near school
description: The streetlight near the local school has been broken for almost a week, leaving the entire area dark and unsafe at night. Students and parents walking back home after evening coaching face difficulties due to poor visibility. Local shop owners also complain about reduced activity after sunset. The absence of light has increased the risk of theft and accidents. Several complaints were made to the local authorities, but no action has been taken yet. The residents are now urging the city corporation to repair or replace the damaged light immediately to ensure safety and restore normal nighttime activity in the neighborhood.

title: Garbage piling up beside market
description: The garbage beside the local market in Mirpur 11 has been piling up for the past three days without collection. The waste includes food scraps, plastic, and packaging materials from nearby shops, creating an unbearable stench. The area has become a breeding ground for flies and mosquitoes, making it difficult for vendors and customers to stay for long. Residents worry that the uncollected waste could cause health issues and attract stray animals. Shop owners claim they have contacted the municipal cleaning team multiple times, but no response has come yet. The community demands urgent cleanup and regular waste collection to keep the market area hygienic.

title: Water leakage damaging road
description: A continuous water leakage from a burst pipe in Dhanmondi 10 has been damaging the road surface for several days. The water flows nonstop, creating puddles and cracks along the main lane. Pedestrians often slip, and vehicles struggle to pass without splashing dirty water. Local shopkeepers complain that their entrances remain wet throughout the day, affecting business. Despite repeated reports to the water authority, no repair work has started yet. The situation worsens every day as the road continues to erode. Residents are urging the authorities to fix the broken pipe immediately before the damage becomes more serious and costly.

title: Open manhole near hospital
description: An open manhole near the hospital in Shyamoli has become a serious safety threat for pedestrians and patients. The cover seems to have been removed weeks ago, leaving a deep, uncovered hole in the middle of the footpath. People walking at night or distractedly using their phones are at high risk of falling in. Hospital staff and nearby residents have placed wooden sticks around it to warn others, but this is not a permanent solution. During rain, the opening becomes invisible due to water accumulation, increasing danger. Locals have reported the issue several times and are requesting an urgent fix from the authorities.

title: Drain blocked by plastic waste
description: The main drain in Banasree has been blocked with plastic waste and debris for days, causing waterlogging after even light rain. Residents have complained that drainage water overflows onto the streets, making it difficult to walk or drive. The stagnant water produces a bad smell and attracts mosquitoes, creating health risks for nearby families. Local shop owners struggle to keep their entrances dry. Despite several calls to the city authority, no cleaning team has visited the area yet. People are requesting an immediate cleanup and better waste management to prevent this recurring issue during the rainy season.

title: Construction debris on footpath
description: A nearby building construction in Mohammadpur has caused piles of sand, bricks, and cement bags to block the public footpath. Pedestrians, especially schoolchildren and elderly people, are forced to walk on the main road, risking accidents. The debris also causes dust pollution, making it uncomfortable for people living nearby. Residents have complained to the contractor several times, but the materials are still left there carelessly. The situation worsens during rain as the mud spreads across the walkway. Locals are demanding strict enforcement of construction waste disposal rules to keep the footpath clean and accessible for all pedestrians.

title: Garbage truck leaking waste
description: Residents in Khilgaon have noticed that a garbage truck regularly leaks waste and foul-smelling liquid while moving through the streets. The spilled waste attracts stray dogs and flies, creating an unhygienic environment. The road becomes slippery and smelly, causing discomfort to pedestrians and shop owners. Locals believe the truck’s container is damaged or improperly sealed. They have repeatedly requested the waste management team to fix the issue, but no action has been taken. People are now urging the city authority to inspect all garbage trucks and ensure proper maintenance to prevent further environmental pollution.

title: Street flooded after small rain
description: In Rampura, a small amount of rainfall is enough to flood the main street due to poor drainage. Water quickly accumulates, reaching ankle-deep levels and staying for hours. Commuters face major difficulties as rickshaws and bikes struggle to pass through. Residents complain that this problem repeats every time it rains, yet no cleaning or repair work has been done. The blocked drains are filled with plastic and dirt. Many fear that prolonged waterlogging will damage the road permanently. Locals urge the city authorities to clear the drainage system and ensure proper flow to prevent repeated flooding.

title: Open garbage dumping site
description: An open garbage dumping site in Jatrabari has turned into a serious health hazard. Residents throw household waste there daily, and no collection truck visits regularly. The area emits a foul odor and attracts flies, rats, and stray animals. During rain, the waste spreads onto the nearby road, making it slippery and dirty. Locals have requested the city authority to install covered bins and enforce proper waste disposal rules. The community is worried about spreading diseases if the problem continues. Immediate cleaning and fencing of the dumping area are necessary to restore hygiene and safety for residents.

title: Fallen electric pole blocking road
description: A fallen electric pole has been blocking the road in Tejgaon since a recent storm. The pole is lying across one side of the street, restricting vehicle movement and posing a serious safety hazard. Electric wires are still attached, sparking occasionally during rain. Drivers are forced to take longer routes, creating traffic jams nearby. Local authorities were informed immediately, but no removal work has started yet. Residents are concerned that the loose wires could cause electrocution. They urge the electricity department to remove the pole and restore safe traffic flow before any serious accident occurs.
